why: Two rounds going out together. The SAFETY round is almost entirely invisible: thirteen older additive migrations become all-or-nothing (no result change, proved by a full iterdump comparison of a fresh install built both ways), a standing lockstep check over the migrations and the corpus passes, the baseline catch-up compares every column it writes, three passes stop deleting waits and storage from a baseline they rewrite, owner filters on the ingredient list and the seasonal list, one shared has-an-image helper, the suite's per-run marker now asks the session's own connection instead of a path, and an app-created recipe records its notes in recipe_notes_original the way an imported one does. The TIME BLOCK round is the one visible change: the block above the ingredients reads in two columns when it has waits, the scaler moves below it, and a conditional second total reads "if you soak". The one database change is migration 063, which drops the retired recipes.notes column. That column has been a derived copy since migration 060, it is outside recipe_snapshots.content, and nothing reads it: the notes themselves are recipe_notes rows and the author's words are in recipe_notes_original. Measured on live read-only: 300 recipes, 95 carrying note rows, 95 carrying originals, and 19 whose derived column no longer agreed with their rows. No row changes, so the byte-equal set and the annotation set both hold still. Three later changes from Andy's click-through: the time block reads in ONE fixed order everywhere (times, Serves, Plan ahead, Keeps); a stated total that is shorter than the waits that always apply has those waits added to it and keeps the author's own figure on a line below, which is 1 recipe of the 300 (earl-grey-tea-cake); and one unreferenced photo is deleted, declared below. The totals change is display only and writes nothing: the rule is planahead.stated_total_verdict, computed at display like every other total. One row changes besides the drop: all-butter-pie-crust gets total_includes_waits = 1, declared under "rows" below. The new rule put it on the review list and could not settle it, and Andy answered it.

rows.why: planahead.stated_total_verdict flagged it as unclear and refused to guess. The recipe states a 1 hr 15 min total with a 1 hr chill that always applies and NO cook time, so the rule has no prep + cook + waits upper bound to compare the stated total against. Andy read the recipe and answered it: 15 min hands-on plus the 1 hr chill IS the stated 1 hr 15 min, so the author counted the wait. The crust alone is never baked, which is why cook_time is empty and why the arithmetic was unavailable to the rule rather than merely inconvenient. This is the second ruling ever recorded on that column, after miso-tofu-recipe's 0 from migration 058's round.
rows.written_by: scripts/add_missed_waits.py, whose TOTAL_RULINGS dict is the one committed home for a ruling and now holds both. Re-running the whole pass is a no-op on everything else and says so in its own printout: 0 waits added, 13 already stored, the 2 ext links rewritten to the values they already hold. Rehearsed 2026-10-07 on a copy of live.
rows.changes_no_figure: recipe_total shows a stated total unchanged, so the page reads '1 hr 15 min' before and after. Measured on the rehearsal copy. What the ruling does is END THE QUESTION, so the recipe leaves reports/total-vs-waits.csv instead of being asked again on every survey. The survey then finds nothing and writes no list at all.
rows.checked_by: the command block in golive/2026-10-07-drop-notes-column.md section 3b, which diffs every cell of recipes between the before and after copies and fails unless exactly this one moved. WARNING: scripts/gates/rounds.py does NOT check it. 'recipes' is in tables.except because 063 drops a column from it, and an excepted table is not compared at all, so the gate is blind to every other cell of it for this round. That block is what closes the hole the exception opens.

files.why: The only unreferenced file in the photo library besides README.txt. 119,394 bytes, 768 x 1024, created 2026-07-31 11:42, and byte-identical to adventist-gumbo.jpg, which IS referenced (cook_photos.path). So its name is one recipe and its content is another recipe's cook photo. The cauliflower recipe has image NULL in live and in all 12 backups, the oldest from 2026-09-29, and no backup references the file.
conditions: a copy is in backups/ before anything is deleted
its sha256 still equals static/images/adventist-gumbo.jpg's, read from live's own folder
no row of recipes.image, cook_photos.path or library_sourced_content.sourced_image names it
files.checked_by: the command block in golive/2026-10-07-drop-notes-column.md section 4, which exits non-zero unless all three hold. WARNING: scripts/gates/rounds.py does NOT read this key. It compares databases, and a photo is a file. The declaration is here so the round's record names exactly one file, and the checking is a command a person runs and reads.
